content:
You draft referral notes that a primary care provider (PCP) sends to a specialist. The PCP will review, edit and sign your draft, so write it in the PCP's voice, ready to send.

The reader is a specialist who has never met this patient and is triaging many referrals. They need to know quickly why the patient is being sent now, what question the PCP wants answered, what has already been tried or worked up, and anything that would change how they manage the patient. Lead with that. Leave out chart content this specialist has no use for.

Your source is a structured chart extract plus whatever the PCP typed, including their answers to follow-up questions. Every clinical statement in the note must come from one of those. The extract has no free-text notes, so symptoms, examination findings, functional status and patient preferences are absent unless the PCP supplied them; do not supply them yourself. When something this specialist would expect is missing, a follow-up question was left unanswered, or two entries in the chart disagree, say so in the final section so the PCP can fill it in before sending. A note that reads complete but contains an invented detail is worse than one with a visible gap.

Give dates for results and events. For a trend, state the direction with the first and latest values and their dates rather than listing every reading.

Format: plain text with no markdown, because the draft goes into an editable text field. Put each section heading in capitals on its own line, in this order:

REASON FOR REFERRAL
CLINICAL QUESTION
RELEVANT HISTORY
CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
KEY RESULTS
WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING

If the PCP gave no clinical question, propose the one the data best supports and mark it "[suggested - confirm]". Aim for one page, roughly 250 to 400 words. Start directly with the first heading; do not add a greeting, sign-off or commentary about the draft.

<referral_request>
Referring to: Cardiology
Referral condition: Ischemic heart disease / chronic heart failure
Urgency: urgent
PCP's clinical question: (none given)
PCP's additional notes: Reason for referral now: worsening breathlessness over two weeks, now breathless after walking across a room, with new swelling of both ankles. She is sleeping on three pillows.
</referral_request>

<what_this_specialist_needs>
The cardiologist will want: the cardiac diagnoses with dates, prior events and interventions (MI, PCI, CABG, heart failure admissions), latest ejection fraction and cardiac imaging, current cardiac medications (antiplatelet, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic) and obvious gaps in them, blood pressure and heart rate, lipid and glycemic control, renal function and potassium, recent emergency or inpatient encounters, and smoking status.
</what_this_specialist_needs>

Write the referral note.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Urgent referral for an 85-year-old woman with known ischemic heart disease (CABG 2009) and chronic heart failure (EF 39.2% in 05/2025). Over the past two weeks she has had worsening breathlessness, now on walking across a room, with new bilateral ankle swelling. She is sleeping on three pillows. She had an ICU admission for heart failure in 11/2025.

CLINICAL QUESTION
[suggested - confirm] Does she have decompensated heart failure needing urgent reassessment (repeat echo, diuretic and GDMT optimization), and how should her regimen be managed given persistent low blood pressure and reduced eGFR?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease 2009-08-17; CABG 2009-08-30. Clopidogrel, metoprolol, simvastatin and nitroglycerin spray started 2009-08-24.
- Chronic congestive heart failure, diagnosed 2025-04-27. NYHA assessment done that day (class not in extract).
- Emergency visit and ICU admission 2025-11-22 for heart failure; IV furosemide 2025-11-22 to 2025-12-06. Heart failure education 2025-12-07.
- Type 2 diabetes since 2004; CKD (stage 2 on problem list), microalbuminuria.
- Never smoked.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
Metoprolol succinate 100 mg and carvedilol 25 mg are both listed as active. Losartan 50 mg, furosemide 40 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, simvastatin 20 mg, nitroglycerin spray, metformin ER 500 mg, alendronate 10 mg. Furosemide, carvedilol, losartan, metformin and alendronate show start dates of 2026-11-09. No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- LV EF 39.2% (echo 2025-05-26). No later echo.
- BP: systolic 85/46 on 2026-11-16; systolic 79 to 92 since 2026-09-21 (108/68 in 2017). HR 61 on 2026-11-09.
- NT-proBNP: 1963 (2025-04-27), peak 1869 (2025-12-02), 1584 (2025-12-06). None this year.
- eGFR 36.2, creatinine 1.4 on 2026-11-09 (eGFR 62.5 on 2026-10-19, 30.5 on 2026-06-29; 100.6 in 2017). K 4.5 on 2026-11-09.
- LDL 96.3 mg/dL on 2026-11-09 (range 85 to 145 this year). HbA1c 5.4% on 2026-11-09.
- Weight 77.6 kg, unchanged across all recorded values this year.
- Troponin I recorded as 0 on all readings through 2025-12-06.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Echo 2025-05-26, stress test 2025-04-27, ECGs 2025-04-27 and 2025-11-22, chest radiograph 2025-11-22 (reports not in extract). Heart failure telemedicine visits through 2026-11-16. No work-up for the current symptoms is documented.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy on anti-VEGF injections (latest 2026-09-28), diabetic neuropathy, osteoporosis, anemia.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Clinical question was not given; the one above is suggested.
- Both metoprolol succinate and carvedilol are active; confirm whether this duplication is intended.
- Chart lists a hospice admission 2026-07-06 for heart failure, yet she is on active care. Confirm her current status and goals of care.
- Oxygen saturation is recorded as 79% on every reading in 12/2025; likely a data artifact. Please give a current value.
- Current examination findings, vitals, weight and any labs or ECG from this episode are not in the extract.
- NYHA class, echo report details and the CABG graft details are not available.
- Chart BMI/obesity finding (30+) conflicts with BMI 27.5.
- Medication review is flagged as due; no ACE inhibitor/ARNI, MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor is listed, and the reasons are not recorded.
